what_i_could_not_do: I TOOK NO HARDWARE FRAMES AND RENTED NO POD. Every image and every number in this piece comes from an OFFLINE rasteriser I wrote (`tools/visual/f10-r6-visible-surface.mjs`), which builds the shipped actor in Node, poses it through the game's own `poseFromRig`, and z-buffers it. It is the same geometry and the same pose code the game runs, and it is NOT the game's renderer: no shadows, no ambient occlusion, no textures, no post, and a two-term light I chose. So my claim is precisely 'the geometry the camera can see has changed, in these ways, by these amounts', and it is NOT 'the game looks like this'. A GPU capture through `f10-r5-appearance.mjs` on the same two arms would settle what I cannot, and the whole point of the r5 pack is that it now exists and costs $0.026.

MY FIRST TWO CUTS OF THE FACE WERE WORSE THAN THE EGG THEY REPLACED AND ONLY LOOKING CAUGHT IT. Cut 1 put the eyeball 7 mm proud inside a full 8-arc orbit ring and rendered a gargoyle in goggles. Cut 2 flattened it and still read as a mask made of cables. Both passed every number I had — eye pixels went from 0 to thousands in both — because a visible-pixel census cannot tell a face from a lumpy mask. I only found it by rendering the thing and opening the file. THAT IS THE SAME LESSON RI-VIS08 B2 STATES: statistics can fail a build and can never pass one. If I had shipped cut 1 the census in this file would have looked identical.

MY OWN PREVIEW LIED TO ME TWICE AND BOTH LIES WERE ABOUT THE THING I WAS TUNING. (1) It shaded flat, so every 7-segment landmark tube read as a hard-edged cable and I nearly tuned the landmarks to compensate for a defect in my instrument; the game ships smooth normals, so I added normal interpolation and re-judged. Both are fixed and both are commented in the tool. A third such error I have not found would look exactly like these two.

THE HOLE CLAUDE.md NAMES IS STILL A HOLE AND THIS ROUND SAT IN IT. The character directive's requirement 4 says RI-VIS08 §D stops at fidelity and NOTHING IN THE CORPUS COVERS CHARACTER DESIGN. headline: Both defects were the SAME defect the hands had, and neither was in the geometry. The player's feet were 68 mm UNDERGROUND: the presentation IK pinned the ankle to `groundY + 0.02` when the rig puts it at 0.090 and the sole hangs 88 mm below the bone, so round 4's heel, sole, ball and three clawed toes were drawn every frame into the dirt — which is exactly why r5's two arms were byte-identical there. And the humanoid face was not featureless, it was ENCLOSED: the eye sat 5.8 mm inside the skull ellipsoid with 0.7 mm of pupil clearing it, the brow ridge 6.9 mm in, the orbit rim 13.8 mm in and the nasal bridge 28.8 mm in — with a second, independent bug scaling head-attached pieces by `build` on top of a headScale that already solves for build, which put the eyes of 52 of 148 humanoid NPCs at literally ZERO visible pixels and the eyes of the heavy variants on stalks.

feet.what: `poseFromRig`'s terrain conform ended `e[13] = gy + .02` — a constant pin, 2 cm above the ground.
feet.why_that_is_wrong: `game/data/combat/skeleton.json` places `foot_l` at world y 0.0900 in rest, and `buildSkeleton`'s own foot block states its own number: 'the sole's underside has to land at foot-local y = -0.088'. So the pin dropped the bone 70 mm and took the whole foot with it.
feet.measured_not_reasoned: The shipped player posed through `poseFromRig`, reading the skinned world y of every vertex whose dominant influence is `foot_l`: WITHOUT the conform `skin@foot_l` spans y 0.0020..0.1539 (sole 2 mm above ground); WITH it, -0.0680..0.0839 (sole 68 mm below), and `bone@foot_l` — the 36 claw vertices — spans -0.0466..-0.0302, entirely underground.
feet.why_r5_saw_no_difference: Both of r5's arms had their feet under the terrain, so replacing the foot geometry changed nothing a camera could see. The flat floating cap in `04-feet-player.png` is the CLOTH calf, which is not conformed and therefore stops at the rest ankle 81 mm above the grass while the foot is beneath it.
feet.the_fix: `e[13] += clamp(gy - groundY, -0.25, 0.25)` — a DELTA, not a pin. On flat ground the shift is exactly zero, which is the correct null a pin can never have; on a slope or a stair each foot rides its own terrain. It also stops overwriting the animated vertical motion of the foot with a constant, which is what flattened every heel strike and toe-off. Clamped to a stair riser so a deck or boardwalk above the terrain field cannot swallow the leg.
feet.acceptance: The brief's condition was 'the foot frames stop being byte-identical'. 24 of 24 foot frames differ between the arms (8 bearings x 3 pitches), against r5's 0 of 3 static and 1 of 8 walking on hardware. Visible `skin@foot_l` pixels over 8 bearings: 30,984 -> 37,981, and the three clawed toes go from invisible to the most legible thing at the end of the leg (sheet 01).

face.bug_1_landmarks_authored_against_a_typed: The skull is an ellipsoid; the landmarks were typed-in z constants. Solving the ellipsoid for its own surface height above each landmark's (x, y) — head-local metres, before headScale: eye front 0.0870 vs surface 0.0928 = 5.8 mm BURIED; pupil 0.0936 = 0.7 mm proud; brow ridge inner end 6.9 mm buried; orbit rim top 13.8 mm buried; nasal bridge upper end 28.8 mm buried; mandible line 27.6 mm buried inside the JAW mass, which it was never measured against. The only features clearing anything were the nose, the ears and the jaw.
face.bug_2_the_scale_was_applied_twice: `addPresentation` computed `bs = M.build * extra`, and head pieces pass `extra = headScale`. But `headScale` ALREADY solves for build — its derivation is `(TARGET_EXTENT - 0.070 * build) / headTopLocal`, written precisely so a heavy character is not a different number of heads tall. Multiplying build back in applied the compensation twice, and only to the head-attached pieces: the skinned skull is scaled by `headScale` alone. `extra` now REPLACES the build scale. Body pieces pass no `extra` and are untouched.
face.the_population: COUNTED, not inherited. `game/data/npcs/*.json`: 408 records with a race, 148 in the humanoid family. `characterFor()` hashes `npc:<eid>` into the base.humanoid pool, and its own filter excludes `hum.drowned` from that pool, so the five reachable variants carry 37/30/29/27/25. The two whose eyes measured ZERO visible pixels — `hum.dunmer-lean` and `hum.imperial-clerk` — carry 52 of the 148, i.e. 35.1%.
face.the_fix: The skull and jaw ellipsoids are named bindings; `faceZ(x,y)` returns whichever mass is in front at that (x,y); every landmark is placed against it with an explicit `proud` in millimetres rather than a `sink` that meant different things for different radii. Lids replace the full orbit ring. The eye is seated 12 mm in so its front stands ~1 mm proud at the centre and falls behind the skull toward its edges, which is what makes the visible patch an almond rather than a circle. A joint ball at every interior ridge joint, for the reason the digit builder has one at every knuckle. A MOUTH, which was absent entirely — two low lips plus a dark seam as a presentation piece. And the JAW was pulled back: it front-faced at z 0.141 against the nose at 0.130, so the most forward point of a human head was its jaw; the order is now nose 0.130 > jaw 0.116 > skull 0.102.
face.acceptance: Eye/pupil/mouth visible pixels over 4 bearings, per shipped variant, BEFORE (pinned 6df8d003) -> AFTER: imperial-clerk 0 -> 3,512; dunmer-lean 0 -> 3,752; drowned 0 -> 3,928; legion-heavy 7,120 -> 2,232; breton-stout 4,438 -> 3,058; marauder 5,691 -> 2,971. Three variants went from nothing to something and the whole family collapsed into one band, which is the point — the spread was the double-scaling. Saxhleel, same fix, same instrument: hive-drone (build 0.80) 0 -> 2,908; deep-warden (build 1.22) 8,398 -> 1,353; player (build 1.00) 1,805 -> 1,805, the exact null.

instruments_built.tools/visual/f10-r6-visible-surface.mjs: The whole actor — body surfaces, equipment, family forms — rasterised orthographically with a z-buffer from arbitrary bearings, with EVERY FRONTMOST PIXEL LABELLED WITH THE PART THAT OWNS IT. Skinned triangles are `<surface>@<dominant bone>`, rigid pieces carry their mesh name. Optionally posed through the game's own `poseFromRig` with a supplied `groundAt`, so the presentation IK is in the measurement rather than assumed away, with the ground plane as a real occluder. Smooth normal interpolation and a shaded mode, because a census cannot tell a face from a mask. Motion via `--clip=locomotion_cycle --phase=`, which drives the same `addPose` the game drives and has no harness verb to get wrong (HAZARDS 16).

hazards_worth_recording: A TOOL THAT LEAVES `group.name` UNSET MEASURES A CHARACTER NOBODY SHIPS. `characterFor()` (actor.js:1867) resolves the morph variant from `group.name` alone, hashing it into the family pool, with `player` special-cased. My first face run left it anonymous, got a variant whose snout swallowed its own eye, and the instrument correctly reported 0 visible eye pixels for a figure that does not exist in the game. It cost about an hour and it would have been a false finding if I had believed it. `character-digit-read.mjs` sets the name; that is why.

A PASSING GATE IS NOT EVIDENCE THAT THE THING IS VISIBLE. `character-digit-read --part=foot` returned 'ok' on 8 of 8 subjects, every day the foot was underground, because it selects by dominant skin weight and so cannot see an occluder that belongs to another bone. Any gate that isolates its subject before measuring it has this shape.
